summary: Lothar von Falkenhausen is a sinologist and historian-archaeologist who taught Sonya S. Lee and Yui Suzuki. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1993 and was a visiting professor at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature in 2003.

Louis Dumont was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Collège d'Harcourt, Institut d'ethnologie, EPHE, and EHESS, training under Marcel Mauss (~1936–1939). He worked at the Musée national des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford, EPHE, and EHESS.

Louis Finot worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, having studied at the École des chartes (1884–1888). He was the first director and organizer of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1900–1930) and held posts at the Collège de France (1920–1935).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post as Dr. at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from around 1977 to 2007.

Louis H. Gray worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton (~1892–1896) and Columbia (~1896–1900), later holding posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1920–1921).

Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and under Michel Bréal and Abel Bergaigne. He held a post at the Collège de France (1885–1925) and taught Antoine Meillet.

Louis Komjathy works in religious studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Boston University (~1999–2005) under Paul Rouzer, and became Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego around 2008.

Louis Ligeti was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1921–1925) and the University of Paris (1925–1928) under Paul Pelliot, and later taught Géza Bethlenfalvy.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, Faculty of Arts of Paris, ENLOV, and under Antoine Meillet. He served as Director at the University of Paris (~1937–1966) and was a member of the Institut de France.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a Belgian scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Liège and under Sylvain Lévi, Hendrik Kern, Charles de Harlez, Philippe Colinet, and Victor Henry, later professing at Ghent and Brussels.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in sinology, linguistics, and Indology, having studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. From around 1795 to 1824, he was Chief Keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale and held an administrative and Persian chair at INALCO.

Louise Child specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD under Linda Hogan at the University of Leeds, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University from around 1978 to 1983 and held a post there around 1993.

Luca Maria Olivieri is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his doctorate from the Free University of Berlin (~2006–2010). He served as director at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente and joined Ca' Foscari University of Venice (~2020).

Lucia Dolce works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015), where she taught Vincent Breugem.
Lucia Galli is a Tibetologist who earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford and held a post at the same institution.
Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from around 1882 to 1887 and later held a post there from around 1893 to 1936.

Luciano Petech worked in Tibetology and archaeology, studying under Giuseppe Tucci. He held posts at Allahabad, Naples "L'Orientale", Sapienza University of Rome, and IsMEO, and served as President of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (attested 1995).

Lucy Annette Jones specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under supervisors Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith间隔Wyschogrod, and also studied under Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (1996–1997).
